old_title: Brighton v Arsenal: Women's Super League - live
new_title: Brighton 0-1 Arsenal: Women's Super League - as it happened
old_text:
We've had a lot of change in the squad. We have spent six or seven weeks together and have come together really well. We lost one game last season in the league and had six draws so this season we have to find ways [to win]. We have to take the first step today. We don't know what Brighton are going to do but we have to be comfortable with the unknown and impose ourselves.
I'm very excited to be here at Brighton. We are going to be very competitive. We have a lot of clarity in this team. And clarity about today's game. So let's go for it.
Georgia Stanway is a very interesting signing for Arsenal. She has called it a "new chapter" and will no doubt be tasked with bringing goals - and forward thrust - from midfield. She has scored heavily at Manchester United and Bayern Munich, and has 32 goals for England. With Little and Caldentey, Arsenal look very strong in the centre of the park this season.
Let's looks at those teams then. For Brighton Lia Walti comes straight into the team after her move from Arsenal so will be highly motivated. Arturo Ruiz has decided to leave fellow new signing Gabby George on the bench.
Arsenal have four new signings in their starting XI. Misa Rodriguez goes straight into goal, while Ona Batlle, Georgia Stanway and Lisa Baum bolster a strong looking lineup with Alessia Russo as the focal point in attack while Kim Little and Mariona Caldentey pull the strings.
It's been an interesting star to the WSL season already, with London City Lionesses beating Manchester United on Friday and Chelsea dropping points yesterday. Catch up right here ...
The WSL is back, with 14 teams this time around as women's football goes from strength to strength. Those pesky upstarts London City Lionesses have been making waves on and off the pitch but it is the old guard who promise another enthralling title race. Champions Manchester City look the team to beat again, although Chelsea have spent heavily in a bid to reclaim their throne. Manchester United could be contenders too, but Arsenal will fancy ther chances of winning the Women's Super League for the first time since 2019.
Renée Slegers' squad has been boosted by the signings of Georgia Stanway, Ona Batlle, Selina Cerci, Géraldine Reuteler, Lisa Baum, Misa Rodríguez, Isabella Damm and Élisa De Almeida. Stanway stands out as in the heart of midfield but could this be the season Olivia Smith really takes off? The Canadian forward joined Arsenal for a then world-record fee of £1m last summer and showed flashes of her potential last season. Her skill and incisive running should give Arsenal's attack an extra dimension during this campaign.
Brighton, under new head coach Arturo Ruiz, offer awkward opponents for the Gunners first up and have designs on a breakthrough season themselves. Dario Vidosic's exit just a week before the start of the season was quite a shock on the south coast but his replacement will be looking to calm the waters and show that Brighton are much more than mid-table also-rans who can be dangerous in the cups.
new_text:
That's it from me. It was a nice day out on the south coast for Arsenal who did just enough to suggest they could be title contenders while Brighton look like they should be fine with Arturo Ruiz despite Dario Vidosic's shock exit. We'll have a WSL roundup in a bit. Thanks for joining and please head over to join Tim de Lisle for live Premier League action of Everton v Manchester United ...
I'll leave you with this email from Stefan Eck on Lisa Baum: "It doesn't surprise me that Lisa Baum needed just eight minutes to adapt to English football! Not much more than one year ago that I saw her score one of the decisive goals for Hamburg's promotion to the Frauen-Bundesliga (against 1. FC Nürnberg). She probably couldn't improve anywhere better than under Renee Slegers. If only her move to the WSL were not another sign of the decline of the Frauen-Bundesliga ... just four years ago, we were so proud that Georgia Stanway had decided to play in Germany. Those days are over."
The atmosphere was brilliant so thank you to all the people who came to support us. We did enough to get at least a point here and there are way more positive things than negative. I'm happy about the work we did. Obviously it's a result we didn't want but we'll be back next week to go for the three points.
For Brighton and Arturo Ruiz, Nnadozie looked as good as ever in goal, Vanegas looked strong at the back and Seike's strong running was a constant menace. Kirby had her moments too.
Renee Slegers will be pleased to leave with the three points, even if she would have liked more goals. Arsenal's new signings impressed and Rodriguez was secure in goal.
Sue Smith on commentary made Georgia Stanway her player of the match but I would say Lisa Baum was the standout player. And it's most decisive one. Think Lauren Hemp or Arjen Robben raiding down the left wing. Speed, skill, trickery with a powerful shot to match. The 19-year-old is a star in the making.
79 min: Walti goes down holding her knee. Ruiz decides it's time for a triple change; Murphy, Tvedten and Garcia are on to make things happen in the last ten.
70 min: Foord wants to remind people that she is still an opetion on Arsneal's left wing despite Baum's heroics. Foord breaks inside and on to her right but lifts her curling effort high and wide.
67 min: Fran Kirby releases Kiko Seike with a lovely pass down the right. Her shot is deflected out for a corne,r which is punched clear by a commanding Rodriguez.
59 min: Baum carves her way from the left through the heart of the Brighton defence, leaving defenders trailing. It opens up and she lefts fly with her right foot but it dribbles through to the keeper. Interesting that the German teenager can go both ways though. A superb trait for a winger.
56 min: Olivia Smith is exactly the type of winger Mikel Arteta loves in the Arsenal men's side. Tenacious and defensively responsible as well as able to beat her full-back
50 min: Apologies. Sky just binned off the game on main event so after some scrabbling around i can see it again. No goals so far in the second half thankfully.
I think Ruiz will be pretty satisfied with his first 45 minutes as Brighton manager. His side couldn't do much about Baum's goal and they didn't fold after it happened. They grew into the game and looked like they could produce something on the counter.
The teams go into the interval. Lisa Baum's magnificent individual goal lit up an engrossing half. I'll grab a cuppa while the players have their oranges. Back soon.
43 min: Stanway releases Smith down the right. One, then two stepovers from the Canadian signal danger but Brighton defend well. 90 seconds in the half to go.
38 min: Almost a mix-up between Catley and Rodriguez at the back but they escape. without harm. Hope for Brighton here now. Arsenal getting aa little slack in their passing.
